summary: Client-only results of the 'mon' debug monitor's mon::WallDebugRequestComponent. Registered by bg3.exe+0x11EF2C0 (size 0x18); its destructor bg3.exe+0xA51A80 is 'add rcx, 8; jmp bg3.exe+0x5946C0' = the plain-Array destructor applied at +8. The default constructor puts a 16-bit default id (global DAT_1461766d0, the same 'none' value the game uses for a short handle in esv::GameplayController and ecl::CharacterTask_Spell) at +0. No system of the shipped binaries fills or reads it; the array's element type cannot be established. Never seen alive.

fields.name: field_0
fields.evidence: default constructor bg3.exe+0x11F1170 (slot 3 of ops table bg3.exe+0x5567260) zeroes the quadword then stores the 16-bit global DAT_1461766d0 at +0 (macOS default constructor: strh at +0). That global is the 'unset' value of a 16-bit id compared in esv::GameplayController::EnterCombat (+0x48) and ecl::CharacterTask_Spell::Clear (+0x328).

fields.name: _Pad2
fields.evidence: padding up to the 8-aligned array; zeroed by the constructor's quadword store.

fields.name: Data
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0xA51A80 (disassembled: add rcx,8; jmp 0x1405946C0) destroys a plain Array at +8: buffer freed when capacity != 0, no per-element work; element type unknown.

fields.name: Capacity
fields.evidence: Array capacity at +0x10 (bg3.exe+0x5946C0 via the +8 thunk); constructor zeroes it.

fields.name: Size
fields.evidence: Array size at +0x14; constructor bg3.exe+0x11F1170 stores 0 there.

open_questions: What the 16-bit id at +0 is (shared 'none' value DAT_1461766d0).
Element type and stride of the array at +8 - no producer in the shipped binaries.
status_reason: no live or captured instance: needs a situation that creates it
second_pass: Cannot be settled from code: the second pass found no producer or consumer anywhere - bg3.exe has only the type registration (App::CreateECS -> bg3.exe+0x11EExxx), the static type-name initialiser and the component ops; the macOS build has only ComponentOps/ComponentSignals/destructor instantiations (macos_index.py names '<mon::' lists just the eight mon types) and the Toolkit DLLs mention them only in App::AddGlobalSwitchesToOptionDialog. The shapes from the creator/destructor stand; the members stay unknown.
